For Applicant : Shri Dinesh Yadav, Advocate on behalf of Shri Anuroop Panda, Advocate For Respondent/State : Ms Sunita Sahu, PL

For Complainant/prosecutrix : Shri Anuj Kumar Pandey,
Advocate on behalf of Shri Rajendra Patel, Advocate ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 11.11.2024 1.
Heard on the application filed under Section 439 of the CrPC.
This is the first bail application before this Court filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail.

2. The applicant has been arrested on 12.05.2024 in connection with Crime No.219 of 2024,
registered at PS-Khairagarh, District-Khairagarh- Chhuikhadan-Gandai, Chhattisgarh for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the IPC, and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 (PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES) Mcrc 4337 of 2024 3.

entities.text: POCSO Act, 2012 (PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES) Mcrc 4337 of 2024
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 09.05.2024, father of the prosecutrix has lodged a missing report that his minor daughter is missing since 08.05.2024, and her whereabouts could not be traced out.
Police has registered the offence under Section 363 of the IPC against unknown person.
During the investigation, prosecutrix was recovered on 12.05.2024 from possession of the applicant, thereafter, he was arrested.
After investigation, charge-sheet was filed for offence under Sections 363, 366A, 376(2)(n) of the IPC, and Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that prosecutrix is a major girl, having love affair with the applicant.

She herself eloped with the applicant on her own will, and resided with him for Ghanshyam Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31422570/
1 about three days, and not complained to any one.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Prosecutrix
has been examined before the learned trial Court as PW2 and has not supported the prosecution case.
Rather, she stated in her evidence that she herself had gone with the applicant and having love affair with him.
He would also submit that there is no legally admissible evidence with respect to age of the prosecutrix that she was minor on the date of incident.
Applicant is in jail since 12.05.2024, therefore, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned State counsel as well as learned counsel for the prosecutrix/objector opposes the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.
However, it is not in dispute that prosecutrix has been examined before the learned trial Court as PW2, has turned hostile, and has not supported the prosecution case.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, also considering nature of allegations against the applicant, as well as material collected during the investigation, further, that the prosecutrix has been examined as PW2 before the learned trial Court, has turned hostile and has not supported the case of prosecution, applicant is in jail since 12.05.2024, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

8. Accordingly, the bail application filed by the applicant- Ghanshyam Verma s/o Shankar Verma, is allowed and he shall be released on bail on his executing a personal bond in sum of Rs.25,000/-
with one surety of like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, for his appearance on each date of hearing of the case during trial, unless exempted by the learned trial Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
(Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) JUDGE padma Ghanshyam Verma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31422570/
